title.rendered: Nigeria Innovation Summit 2026 to spotlight AI, emerging technologies in Lagos

content.rendered:
With just days to go, all is set for the 11th edition of the Nigeria Innovation Summit (NIS), as innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, investors, technology leaders, researchers, business executives and development stakeholders from Nigeria and around the world prepare to converge in Lagos to explore how AI and emerging technologies can accelerate development across Africa.

Themed “Innovating in the Age of AI,” the 2026 Summit will hold on Tuesday, October 6, at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, Lagos. The hybrid summit will provide both physical and virtual participation opportunities.

At the heart of NIS 2026 will be conversations around the opportunities and challenges presented by artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. One of the major panel sessions, “AI for Africa: Transforming Education, Agriculture and Healthcare at Scale,” will examine how AI can be applied to address some of Africa’s most pressing development challenges and expand access to better services, knowledge and opportunities.

Another major conversation, “Building Trusted AI for Africa: Policy, Regulation, Data Governance, and Investment for the Future,” will focus on the frameworks, safeguards, investments and partnerships required to develop and deploy AI responsibly across the continent.

The summit will also explore the broader implications of AI for business transformation, entrepreneurship, digital infrastructure, innovation policy, research commercialisation, inclusion and the future of work.

NIS 2026 will feature an impressive line-up of public-sector leaders, technology executives, entrepreneurs, innovators and global thought leaders.

Among the distinguished speakers listed for the summit are Engr. Rasheed O. Ojulari, Chief Innovation Officer, NNPC Limited, Research, Technology and Innovation; Jara Pascual, CEO, Collabwith; Nelson T. Ajulo, CEO/CTO and Co-Founder, MyHives; Ngozi Aderibigbe, Partner, Gray & Silicon Legal Advisors; Michael Pepper, AI Systems and Personal Branding Strategist; Kevin Eze, Founder, SounDisruptr and African Food Network; Bisola Fasanya, Founder, Atel Q; and Ademola Osindero, Founder, Stackchase Limited.

Also featured are Olufunke Olufon, Founder/Principal Consultant, Iwà Consulting; Toyosi Badejo-Okusanya, CEO/Founder, Adaptive Atelier; Bharat Kundra, Programme Specialist, GenU 9JA, UNICEF Nigeria; Dr. Goodluck Nnorom, Strategic Leadership Researcher and Entrepreneur; Engr. Alex Omaghomi, Group CEO, Zilex Holdings and Hostplace Group; and other leading voices from across Africa’s innovation ecosystem.

The breadth of the speaker line-up reflects the summit’s focus on bringing together different perspectives around the intersection of technology, innovation, business, policy and development.

NIS 2026 highlights include insightful presentations by thought leaders and industry experts; Nigeria Innovation Experience Talks (NiX Talks) — a series of focused, high-impact presentations from innovators challenging the status quo; Exhibitions and product demonstrations; innovation showcases, providing opportunities for innovators and organisations to demonstrate solutions; networking sessions connecting entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, businesses and ecosystem stakeholders; and Innovation Tours, offering selected delegates an opportunity to experience innovative organisations and technology environments.

The awards will bring together business leaders, innovators, government representatives, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders to celebrate innovation and recognise contributions that are helping to advance technology, enterprise and development in Nigeria.

According to Tony Ajah, Programme Director, Nigeria Innovation Summit, the 2026 edition comes at an important moment as AI increasingly reshapes industries, businesses and societies.

“This year we will explore how AI and emerging technologies can accelerate national development, transform industries, improve public services, strengthen businesses, and create new opportunities for millions of Africans. AI is not just a tool; it’s a seed. And those who recognise it early, plant it wisely, and harness its surplus will rise.”

Ajah added, “As a nation blessed with a youthful population, entrepreneurial spirit, and abundant talent, Nigeria has an opportunity to become not just a consumer of AI technologies but a creator of solutions that address local challenges and compete globally.”

Attendance at the summit is free, but registration is required for physical participation.

The summit will also be available virtually, enabling participants beyond Lagos and Nigeria to join the conversations.

title.rendered: WEDDING POLICE: Noble Igwe brings fashion, media experience

content.rendered:
Popular wedding entertainment show from the Wedding Channel, Wedding Police, has concluded plans to commence its next chapter, with media personality, entrepreneur and style figure Noble Igwe joining the show.

The development comes as Nigerian weddings become bigger cultural and fashion moments, with Wedding Police evolving alongside them.

The show is returning to the air with a new focus on the people, personalities, style choices and conversations that make weddings such a significant part of African social culture.

Igwe’s addition is significant not simply because he brings another voice to the hosting line-up, but because his longstanding relationship with fashion, media and popular culture gives him a unique lens through which to engage with the evolving world of Nigerian weddings.

The new Wedding Police season is therefore not simply about deciding whether an outfit gets a pass or gets called out. It is about looking at the culture behind the clothes: the creativity that goes into dressing for a wedding and the trends that emerge from wedding seasons.

Over the years, Nigerian weddings have grown into some of the country’s biggest social and fashion gatherings. From elaborate traditional ceremonies to contemporary white weddings, they have become spaces where people express their identities, experiment with style and, occasionally, compete for the unofficial title of best-dressed guest.

title.rendered: EBA celebrates two years of building brands

content.rendered:
Eni Brand Architect (EBA), a Lagos-based architectural PR, marketing and communications agency, is celebrating its second anniversary, marking two years of building brands through strategic communication, compelling storytelling and culturally relevant ideas.

Founded in September 2024 by Enitan Eniola Omoniyi, popularly known as Eniivy, EBA was established with a clear vision: to approach brand building as an intentional process, combining strategy, creativity and communication to help brands develop stronger identities and lasting relevance.

In two years, that vision has evolved into a growing agency with experience across public relations, marketing, digital communications, social media management, content production, creative strategy, media relations, crisis management, events and brand storytelling.

EBA’s work over the past two years has spanned organisations, businesses, initiatives, events and personal brands across different sectors.

The agency has delivered its prowess and talent for projects such as Play With Stephen, an African golf initiative focused on autism awareness and inclusion; MediaReach OMD, a leading media agency; Omodaadaa Foundation, a non-government organization tasked with tackling humanitarian needs; as well as projects across outdoor advertising, events, digital campaigns, community platforms and personal branding.

This breadth has allowed EBA to develop an approach that is not limited to a single industry. Instead, the agency works to understand the individual objectives, audience and identity of each client before developing the strategy and creative direction required to communicate effectively.

For EBA, the objective is not simply to help brands occupy more space, but to make that space meaningful. The anniversary represents a milestone in the agency’s journey, but also the beginning of its next phase of growth.

“EBA has always been about building, We are building brands, we are building ideas, we are building relationships, and we are building a team that understands that good a identity can influence how people see and experience a brand. Two years gives us something to celebrate, but it also gives us a foundation to build from.” Eniola Omoniyi added.

EBA’s secondanniversary comes as the agency continues its commitment to helping brands tell better stories, communicate with greater intention and build lasting relevance in an increasingly competitive marketplace.

title.rendered: EBA celebrates two years of building brands

content.rendered:
Lagos, Nigeria — September 2026 — Eni Brand Architect (EBA) is celebrating its second anniversary. The milestone marks two years of helping brands build stronger identities, improve visibility, and connect with the right audiences.

EBA was founded in September 2024 by Enitan Eniola Omoniyi, popularly known as Eniivy. Since then, the company has grown into a creative and communications agency serving brands, organisations, founders, and professionals.

The EBA second anniversary is both a celebration of progress and a look at what comes next.

Two Years of Building With Purpose

From the beginning, EBA has focused on helping brands communicate with greater clarity.

The agency believes that visibility alone is not enough. A brand also needs to be understood, trusted, and remembered.

As a result, EBA combines strategy, communication, media, marketing, and creative execution. Each project starts with the needs of the brand rather than a fixed formula.

This approach has helped EBA support clients across different industries and stages of growth.

Growing Across Branding, PR and Marketing

Over the past two years, EBA has expanded its work across several areas.

These include brand strategy, public relations, digital marketing, advertising, content production, social media, media relations, events, and creative communication.

The agency has also worked on projects such as Play With Stephen, MediaReach OMD, and Omodaadaa Foundation.

Each project has required a different approach. However, the goal remains the same: help the brand communicate clearly and reach the people who matter.

Turning Ideas Into Experiences

EBA’s work goes beyond online visibility.

The company has supported campaigns, events, outdoor advertising, media activities, digital communication, and community-focused projects.

For EBA, every project starts with a simple question:

What should people understand, feel, or do after experiencing this brand?

The answer then shapes the strategy.

In some cases, the brand may need stronger positioning. In others, it may need better content, wider media exposure, a campaign, or a well-executed event.

By connecting these different areas, EBA helps brands create more consistent experiences.

A Milestone for the Team

The second anniversary also reflects the growth of the people behind EBA.

Founder Enitan Eniola Omoniyi described the journey as one built around brands, ideas, relationships, and people.

For the company, the milestone is not only about looking back. It is also an opportunity to prepare for the next stage.

EBA plans to continue building stronger relationships, expanding its capabilities, and helping more brands improve how they communicate.

Looking Ahead

As the agency enters its third year, EBA remains focused on helping brands become more visible and more relevant.

The company will continue to support businesses, organisations, and professionals through strategy, communication, marketing, media, and creative execution.

The first two years have created a strong foundation.

Now, EBA is building on it.

About Eni Brand Architect

Eni Brand Architect (EBA) is a Lagos-based brand, communications, and marketing company.

EBA helps brands strengthen their positioning, improve visibility, and build meaningful relationships with their audiences.

Its services include brand strategy and positioning, public relations and communication, marketing and advertising, media production and event coverage, content and creative strategy, B2B solutions, and website development and management.

Want to build a stronger brand?

Explore EBA’s services or contact the team to start a conversation.

title.rendered: Leading Brands Unite for Swing for Autism 2026 at Lakowe Lakes

content.rendered:
Corporate partners joined Play With Stephen to promote autism awareness and support centres providing diagnosis, therapy and education across Africa

LAGOS, NIGERIA — 25 AUGUST 2026 — Play With Stephen successfully concluded the seventh edition of Swing for Autism 2026, held from 21–23 August at Lakowe Lakes Golf & Country Estate in Lagos.

The three-day tournament brought together golfers, corporate partners, autism advocates, volunteers and families around one shared purpose: using golf to raise awareness and support the autism community.

Founded by Stephen Onaivi in 2020, Swing for Autism has grown from a golf tournament into a wider advocacy platform. The initiative uses sport to start important conversations about autism and generate support for centres providing diagnosis, therapy and education to autistic individuals and their families.

Corporate Partnerships Power the Tournament

The success of Swing for Autism 2026 reflected the commitment of several organisations that contributed resources, expertise, products, services and media support.

Participating brands and partners included Olston Foundation, EBA, Simply Black, Golf GameBook, Devtraco, Guinness, Lakowe Lakes, The Wheatbaker, Mixtah Africa, The Singleton, Pepsi, Aquafina, Fortress Capital, Spur and Indomie.

GHM Luxury, MTN and RewindFM Lagos also supported the event and helped extend its message beyond the golf course.

Olston Foundation and EBA played leading roles in the planning and delivery of the tournament. Their support covered important aspects of the preparation and execution required to bring the seventh edition to life.

Golf GameBook supported tournament scoring and results, helping players and organisers follow the competition throughout the event.

Each partnership contributed to a complete tournament experience while drawing greater public attention to autism awareness and inclusion.

Golf With a Purpose Beyond Competition

Swing for Autism is built on the belief that golf can achieve more than producing winners on the course. It can bring people together, open conversations and direct attention towards causes that often receive limited public support.

Across Africa, many autistic individuals and their families continue to face difficulties accessing diagnosis, therapy, education and reliable guidance. Play With Stephen responds to this need by directing tournament proceeds to beneficiary centres already providing these essential services.

The support received from corporate partners allows the initiative to reach wider audiences and strengthen the organisations working directly with autistic individuals and their families.

By supporting Swing for Autism 2026, participating brands became part of a movement that connects sport, advocacy and community impact.

A Growing Platform for Autism Advocacy

Since its first edition in 2020, Play With Stephen has continued to expand the reach of Swing for Autism. The tournament provides a meeting point for golfers, businesses, advocates and members of the autism community who want to contribute to a more informed and inclusive society.

The 2026 edition marked another important step in that journey. It demonstrated what can happen when brands move beyond visibility and use their influence, resources and platforms to support a meaningful cause.

The tournament’s partnership story also received coverage from The Guardian Nigeria, extending its message to audiences beyond the event.

Play With Stephen thanks every sponsor, partner, golfer, volunteer, advocate and guest who contributed to the success of Swing for Autism 2026.

The tournament may have ended, but the work continues. Every partnership strengthens the mission, every conversation increases understanding and every swing helps move autism advocacy forward.

For more information about Play With Stephen and its autism advocacy initiatives, visit www.pwsgolftournament.com.

About Play With Stephen

Play With Stephen is a sports and social-impact initiative founded by Stephen Onaivi in 2020. Through its annual Swing for Autism golf tournament, the initiative raises awareness and funding for autism care across Africa. It brings golfers, corporate organisations, advocates and community leaders together in support of autism centres and the families they serve.

title.rendered: Why Brand Storytelling Is the Difference Between Being Seen and Being Remembered

content.rendered:
Many brands are talking, but only a few are being remembered.

Every day, audiences encounter countless adverts, social media posts, product launches and promotional offers. In such a crowded space, visibility alone is no longer enough. A brand may attract attention for a moment, but attention does not always create connection.

What makes people remember a brand is the meaning attached to it. That is where brand storytelling becomes important.

Visibility Gets Attention, but Stories Build Connection

Many brands focus their communication on product features, prices and offers. These details matter, but they rarely give audiences a strong reason to care.

People want to understand the purpose behind a brand. They want to know why it exists, what it believes in and how it fits into their lives. A clear story answers these questions and turns ordinary information into something meaningful.

Storytelling gives a product context. It helps audiences see the problem a brand solves, the people it serves and the change it wants to create. Instead of simply presenting what the brand sells, it communicates why the brand matters.

Stories Make Brands Easier to Remember

Audiences may forget the details of an advert, but they often remember how it made them feel.

A strong brand story creates that emotional connection. It gives people something they can recognise, relate to and recall long after a campaign has ended. When the same story runs through a brand’s website, social media, campaigns and customer experience, the brand begins to feel clear and consistent.

That consistency builds familiarity. Familiarity strengthens trust, and trust influences which brands people choose.

Why Many Brands Struggle With Storytelling

Effective storytelling begins with a clear identity. A brand must understand who it is, what it stands for, who it serves and what makes it different.

Without this clarity, communication becomes inconsistent. One campaign says one thing, while the next presents a completely different message. The brand may remain active and visible, but audiences struggle to understand or remember it.

Storytelling also takes time. Unlike a short-term campaign that may produce immediate clicks or sales, a brand story builds value through consistent communication. For this reason, some businesses underestimate it.

However, strong brands are rarely built through isolated promotions. They grow by communicating a clear and recognisable story over time.

Storytelling Is a Strategic Advantage

Brand storytelling is not simply about writing an emotional caption or producing a beautiful video. It is about creating a clear narrative that guides how a brand presents itself across every touchpoint.

A strong story helps a brand communicate with confidence, stand apart from competitors and build a deeper relationship with its audience. It supports campaigns, strengthens positioning and gives every piece of content a clear direction.

That is how authority is established. That is how trust is earned. That is how a brand moves from being noticed to being remembered—and from being remembered to being chosen.

Tell Your Brand Story With EBA

At EBA (Eni Brand Architect), we believe storytelling is not a “nice to have.” It is a strategic advantage.

We help brands uncover what makes them meaningful and turn that clarity into stories that connect with the right audience. From brand strategy and identity to campaigns and digital content, we ensure every message reflects a clear and consistent narrative.

Your brand already has a story. Let us help you tell it the way it deserves to be told.

Ready to build a brand people remember? Contact EBA today.

title.rendered: Swing for Autism: Play With Stephen Mobilises 69 Golfers for Greater Awareness

content.rendered:
Using Golf to Drive Autism Awareness and Community Action

Golfers gathered at the Lakowe Lakes Golf and Country Estate in Lagos for the seventh edition of the Play With Stephen Golf Tournament, using sport as a platform to promote greater autism awareness, understanding and support.

The landmark edition, themed “Swing for Autism,” brought together 69 golfers who shared more than an interest in the game. They came together to demonstrate how sport can create meaningful conversations, mobilise communities and contribute to causes that deserve greater public attention.

The tournament and its autism-awareness mission were featured by ATQ News.

A Landmark Seventh Edition in Lagos

Convened by Stephen Oluwatoyin Onaivi, the Lagos tournament built on six previous editions held in Ghana, where golfers from different countries participated in the initiative.

Bringing the seventh edition to Nigeria marked a significant step in the tournament’s growth and continental journey. It also introduced the Play With Stephen experience to a new community of golfers while maintaining the purpose that has guided the initiative from the beginning.

A total of 69 golfers participated in the Lagos edition, with attendance deliberately managed to remain within the capacity of the golf course and provide a quality tournament experience.

Beyond the competition, every participant became part of a wider effort to increase awareness and encourage more informed conversations about autism.

Golf as a Platform for Advocacy

Play With Stephen is built on the belief that golf can achieve more than recreation and competition. The sport brings people from different professional, social and cultural backgrounds together, creating a valuable network through which important causes can gain greater visibility.

Through the “Swing for Autism” theme, the tournament encourages golfers to use their voices, relationships and influence to promote greater understanding of autism.

Stephen Onaivi’s personal connection to autism has also influenced his decision to use the tournament as a platform for advocacy. His goal is to contribute to solutions for social challenges across African communities, beginning with an issue where increased understanding and support can make a meaningful difference.

The tournament is therefore not defined primarily by who wins. Its greater value lies in the conversations it inspires, the people it informs and the action it encourages.

Awareness Is the Beginning

Although raising awareness remains the initiative’s immediate priority, Play With Stephen has a broader ambition.

“The first thing for us is awareness. The next level is to see how we support centres,” Onaivi explained.

This direction reflects an understanding that awareness must eventually lead to practical action. By helping more people understand autism, the initiative hopes to create a stronger foundation for supporting autism centres, families and communities.

Greater awareness can reduce misunderstanding, encourage inclusion and help people recognise how they can contribute. When golfers, organisations and members of the wider community become more informed, they are better positioned to support initiatives that improve care and expand opportunities.

Building an Informed Golf Community

One of the tournament’s long-term goals is to create a golf community that understands autism and is prepared to take meaningful action.

Imagine the impact if golfers across Nigeria understood autism, recognised the challenges faced by autistic people and their families, and actively contributed to creating solutions. This is the future Play With Stephen hopes to support.

The tournament provides an entry point for this change by combining an established sport with a clear and relatable social purpose. Participants do not simply attend an event; they become part of an expanding advocacy network.

Growing the Movement

Play With Stephen intends to continue the tournament annually while attracting more golfers and expanding its reach across Nigeria and beyond.

Each edition offers another opportunity to introduce new people to the autism-awareness campaign, strengthen existing partnerships and transform sporting participation into wider community impact.

The Lagos edition demonstrated the potential of this approach. Sixty-nine golfers gathered to play, but their presence also amplified a larger message: autism awareness is a responsibility that communities can advance together.

More Than a Tournament

“Swing for Autism” demonstrates that sport can extend beyond entertainment to become a powerful tool for advocacy, inclusion and social change.

By bringing golfers together around a shared purpose, Play With Stephen continues to build a movement in which every game creates an opportunity for awareness and every participant can become an advocate.

The ambition remains clear: continue playing, continue creating awareness and transform that awareness into practical support for autistic people, their families and the centres that serve them.

At Play With Stephen, every swing carries a purpose—and every edition moves the mission forward.

title.rendered: Swing for Autism 2026 Mobilises 69 Golfers for Autism Awareness in Lagos

content.rendered:
Play With Stephen uses golf to raise autism awareness and encourage support for autism centres across Africa

LAGOS, NIGERIA — 25 AUGUST 2026 — Play With Stephen hosted the seventh edition of Swing for Autism 2026 at Lakowe Lakes Golf & Country Estate in Lagos.

The event brought 69 golfers together to raise autism awareness. It also encouraged greater understanding and support for autistic people and their families.

Stephen Onaivi, founder of Play With Stephen, convened the tournament. Previous editions took place in Ghana and attracted golfers from different countries.

This year’s Lagos event continued that journey. It also helped introduce the campaign to a wider audience in Nigeria.

Using Golf to Raise Autism Awareness

Swing for Autism is more than a golf competition. It uses sport to bring people together and start important conversations about autism.

Golf creates opportunities for players, business leaders and community members to connect. Therefore, Play With Stephen uses the game to reach people who can support autism awareness.

Onaivi’s personal connection to autism also shaped the initiative. He saw golf as a practical way to draw attention to a cause that needs wider public understanding.

Sixty-nine golfers took part in the Lagos tournament. Organisers managed the number carefully to suit the capacity of the golf course.

However, the day was not only about scores or winners. Each golfer became part of a wider movement for awareness and inclusion.

Moving From Awareness to Support

For Play With Stephen, awareness is the first step. The wider goal is to turn that awareness into practical support.

“The first thing for us is awareness. The next level is to see how we support centres,” Onaivi told ATQ News.

Autism centres provide important services to autistic people and their families. These services may include diagnosis, therapy, education and family guidance.

Yet many centres need more funding, stronger partnerships and greater public attention. For this reason, Play With Stephen wants to connect them with people and organisations that can help.

The tournament gives autism centres greater visibility. In addition, it encourages golfers and business leaders to learn more about their work.

Building a Community of Informed Golfers

Play With Stephen wants golfers to become active supporters of the autism community.

Better understanding can help people challenge harmful assumptions about autism. It can also encourage more inclusive behaviour at work, at events and in the wider community.

Golfers often have access to strong professional and social networks. As a result, their support can take the autism conversation beyond the golf course.

Swing for Autism 2026 showed this idea in action. The golfers came to play, but they also supported a cause with a wider social purpose.

Growing Swing for Autism Beyond Lagos

Play With Stephen plans to hold the tournament every year. The initiative also aims to welcome more golfers into the autism awareness campaign.

Earlier editions built a strong foundation in Ghana. Now, the Lagos tournament has created another opportunity for growth across Nigeria and Africa.

Looking ahead, Play With Stephen will continue to raise awareness and build partnerships. It will also work towards stronger support for autism centres and families.

ATQ News featured Swing for Autism 2026 and highlighted how the event mobilised golfers for autism awareness.

Play With Stephen thanks every golfer, partner, volunteer and advocate who supported the seventh edition.

The tournament may be over, but the mission continues. Every conversation can increase understanding, and every partnership can create meaningful support.

For more information, visit www.pwsgolftournament.com.

About Play With Stephen

Stephen Onaivi founded Play With Stephen in 2020. The initiative uses golf to promote autism awareness and support autistic people, their families and autism centres across Africa. Its annual Swing for Autism tournament brings golfers, businesses and advocates together for a purpose greater than the game.

title.rendered: Play With Stephen Brings Its Autism Awareness Golf Tournament to Nigeria

content.rendered:
The Play With Stephen autism awareness golf tournament will make its Nigerian debut as the purpose-driven initiative prepares for its landmark seventh edition.

The tournament will take place from August 21 to 23, 2026, at the Lakowe Lakes Golf and Country Club in Lagos. It will bring golfers, sponsors, advocates and families together to promote autism awareness and community inclusion through sport.

After six editions outside Nigeria, the tournament’s arrival in Lagos represents both a major expansion and a meaningful homecoming.

The announcement was also featured by BusinessDay.

Six Editions of Golf with a Purpose

Play With Stephen has spent six editions transforming competitive golf into a platform for autism advocacy.

Each tournament has created opportunities for golfers and other participants to learn about autism, challenge misconceptions and support greater inclusion. As a result, the initiative has grown beyond a sporting event into a community built around awareness and purposeful action.

The seventh edition will continue this mission while introducing it to a Nigerian audience for the first time.

This expansion also reflects the tournament’s growing reach. More importantly, it creates an opportunity to strengthen local conversations about autism and encourage wider community participation.

A Homecoming for Play With Stephen

For Stephen Oluwatoyin Onaivi, Convener of Play With Stephen, bringing the tournament to Nigeria carries personal and organisational significance.

“Bringing the Play With Stephen Golf Tournament to Nigeria for the first time feels like a homecoming,” he explained.

The tournament’s autism-awareness mission is closely connected to his personal experience. Over the years, he has watched golf develop into an effective platform for changing how people understand and discuss autism.

Nigeria’s first edition will therefore build on the progress made during the previous tournaments. At the same time, it will create new opportunities for golfers and communities to contribute to the initiative.

What to Expect at the Tournament

The three-day event will combine competitive golf with activities designed to promote learning, interaction and advocacy.

Participants can expect:

  • Competitive rounds of golf
  • Community engagement activities
  • Autism-awareness conversations
  • Sessions highlighting the experiences of autistic people and their families
  • Opportunities for golfers, sponsors and advocates to connect
  • Discussions about inclusion and practical community support

These activities will ensure that the event remains focused on more than sporting performance. Although competition is an important part of the tournament, its wider purpose is to build understanding and encourage meaningful action.

Why an Autism Awareness Golf Tournament Matters

Sport can bring people together across different professions, backgrounds and communities. Therefore, it can also provide a strong platform for discussing social issues that may not receive enough public attention.

The Play With Stephen autism awareness golf tournament uses this connecting power to challenge harmful misconceptions and encourage greater understanding of autism.

Every golfer who participates can become part of the advocacy effort. Sponsors can also use their platforms and resources to support the message. In addition, families and advocates can share experiences that help others understand the importance of acceptance and inclusion.

Through this approach, the tournament turns participation in sport into an opportunity for learning and social impact.

Supported by Purpose-Driven Partners

The seventh edition has received support from several organisations that recognise the value of sport-led advocacy.

Supporting brands include EBA (Eni Brand Architect), Wheatbaker, Diageo, Pepsi, Lakowe Lakes and MTN, among others.

Their involvement strengthens the tournament’s ability to reach more people and create a well-organised experience. It also demonstrates how businesses can support social causes through partnerships that go beyond conventional sponsorship.

At EBA, we are proud to support an initiative that combines strategy, storytelling, sport and community impact. The tournament reflects our belief that meaningful campaigns should create visibility while also contributing to positive change.

Creating Impact Beyond the Tournament

Play With Stephen’s work continues beyond its annual golf tournament.

The initiative also organises programmes such as the Golf Tasting and Masterclass, which introduces more people to golf while creating additional opportunities for autism awareness and community engagement.

Together, these activities provide different entry points into the movement. Experienced golfers can participate in the tournament, while newcomers can learn about the sport through the masterclass. Advocates, businesses and community members can also contribute through partnerships and awareness campaigns.

This wider approach helps Play With Stephen sustain its message throughout the year.

Swinging for Awareness and Inclusion

The seventh Play With Stephen tournament represents an important stage in the initiative’s journey.

For the first time, the movement will bring its combination of golf, autism advocacy and community engagement to Nigeria. The Lagos edition will also provide a foundation for deeper local partnerships and broader participation.

Above all, the tournament will remind participants that sport can achieve more than entertainment. It can start conversations, challenge misconceptions and encourage people to support a more inclusive society.

Explore more of EBA’s purpose-driven campaigns and brand projects.

This August, Nigeria will not swing only for the game. It will swing for autism awareness, understanding and inclusion.

title.rendered: Ehiz Dadaboy Returns to Radio with New Lounge FM Breakfast Show

content.rendered:
Lounge Network has unveiled Ehiz Dadaboy as the host of its new Lounge FM breakfast show, bringing the viral Radio Is Dead campaign to a memorable conclusion.

For one week, unexplained placards appeared across Lagos, Abuja and Benin City. The message was direct: Radio Is Dead. With no logo or brand name attached, the campaign quickly sparked debates across social media.

However, the conversation was never about announcing the end of radio. Instead, it was designed to challenge that perception and prepare audiences for a new chapter at Lounge Network.

The Mystery Behind Radio Is Dead

The campaign began with a simple but provocative statement. People saw the placards on the streets, shared them online and debated whether radio still had a place in modern Nigerian culture.

Some agreed with the message, while others defended radio as an important source of information, entertainment and connection. Meanwhile, Lounge Network allowed the discussion to grow without immediately revealing its involvement.

This approach turned the audience into active participants. Rather than receiving a conventional advertisement, people helped shape and spread the campaign through their reactions.

Ehiz Dadaboy Returns to the Microphone

Lounge Network eventually ended the speculation with a live on-air reveal. Ehiz Dadaboy entered the studio as the new central host of the Lounge FM Lagos breakfast show.

The reveal video showed him scrolling through the social media posts, arguments and reactions generated by the campaign. He then challenged the original message and declared that radio remained active.

His return brings a familiar voice back to the airwaves. It also signals Lounge FM’s renewed commitment to creating relevant, engaging and audience-focused programming.

The new Lounge FM breakfast show airs on weekday mornings from 6:00 a.m. It combines music, conversations, listener calls and live reactions from the community that helped make the campaign successful.

The announcement and campaign reveal were also covered by The Guardian Nigeria.

More Than One Presenter or Programme

Although Ehiz Dadaboy’s return was central to the reveal, the campaign also reintroduced the wider Lounge Network family.

The network includes Lounge FM Lagos, Lounge FM Abuja, Rewind FM Lagos, Rewind FM Abuja and Bside FM Benin. Each station contributed to the campaign in a way that reflected its audience and identity.

Rewind FM responded with Radio Raised Us, a nostalgic celebration of memorable Nigerian radio moments. Listeners shared stories about important announcements, songs and personalities they first encountered through radio.

Bside FM Benin brought local energy to the conversation through its Radio Don Die response. Its presenters used Nigerian Pidgin and humour to connect with listeners in a familiar voice.

Meanwhile, Lounge FM Abuja prepared its audience for another stage of the network-wide rollout.

These different responses showed that a campaign does not need to speak in one voice everywhere. Instead, each part can adapt to its audience while supporting the same central idea.

The EBA Strategy Behind the Conversation

When Lounge Network approached Eni Brand Architect to amplify the Radio Is Dead campaign, we developed the strategy needed to turn the idea into a wider conversation.

EBA managed the campaign strategy, creative direction, content production, influencer amplification and social media execution. We carefully coordinated each stage so that public curiosity continued to grow without revealing the campaign too early.

The unbranded placards created the initial mystery. Social media content sustained the debate, while influencers introduced different perspectives that encouraged more people to participate.

Finally, the reveal connected every part of the conversation to Lounge Network, Ehiz Dadaboy and the new breakfast show.

The result demonstrates what can happen when a strong idea meets clear strategy, cultural understanding and disciplined execution.

What the Lounge FM Breakfast Show Represents

The campaign did not attempt to prove that radio was dying. Instead, it demonstrated that radio could still surprise people, influence culture and generate conversations across both traditional and digital platforms.

The new Lounge FM breakfast show represents this connection between radio’s established strengths and the changing habits of modern audiences.

Radio remains valuable because it feels immediate and personal. At the same time, digital platforms allow its conversations, presenters and memorable moments to travel far beyond the broadcast signal.

By connecting street activation, social media and live radio, Lounge Network created a campaign that allowed each platform to strengthen the others.

Radio Is Active

The Radio Is Dead campaign began with a statement that divided opinions. It ended by reminding audiences that radio remains active, relevant and capable of evolving.

Ehiz Dadaboy’s return gives Lounge FM Lagos a recognisable personality around which it can build its new morning experience. More importantly, the campaign has shown that radio can still command attention when it understands its audience and communicates creatively.

At EBA, we believe effective campaigns should do more than display a message. They should create conversations that people want to join and experiences they will remember.

Explore our brand, campaign and communication services to discover how EBA helps brands turn strong ideas into meaningful visibility.

If your brand has something worth talking about, let’s create the conversation.

title.rendered: Inside “Radio Is Dead”: A Nigerian Marketing Case Study Worth Teaching

content.rendered:
How EBA Helped Lounge Network Turn Three Words into a Nationwide Conversation

Most campaigns begin by introducing a brand, explaining an offer and asking the audience to take action. Radio Is Dead began with none of those things.

Unbranded placards carrying the provocative statement appeared across Lagos before spreading to Abuja and Benin City. There was no logo, explanation or visible connection to the organisation behind them. As images reached social media, Nigerians began asking questions, challenging the message and debating whether radio had genuinely lost its relevance.

What appeared to be a spontaneous cultural argument was, in fact, a carefully structured campaign developed to generate attention before the launch of a new Lounge FM breakfast show.

The campaign later received national recognition, with THISDAY describing it as a case study worthy of Nigerian marketing classrooms.

EBA’s Role Behind the Campaign

When Lounge Network approached Eni Brand Architect to amplify the Radio Is Dead concept, our responsibility extended beyond generating publicity.

EBA handled the campaign strategy, creative direction, content production, influencer amplification and social media execution that transformed the idea into a coordinated public conversation.

Our task was to build enough curiosity to make people stop, question the message and contribute to the debate without revealing the brand too early. Every stage had to feel natural while remaining strategically connected to the final reveal.

The audience saw placards, reactions and opposing opinions. Behind those public moments was a structured campaign designed around timing, audience behaviour, creative restraint and cultural relevance.

The Strategy of Not Saying Everything

Marketing usually rewards clarity, but strategic communication also requires knowing when information should be revealed.

Radio Is Dead deliberately withheld the identity of the brand and the purpose of the campaign. Instead of immediately explaining the message, the campaign created space for the audience to interpret it.

This absence of information produced curiosity. Curiosity encouraged conversation, and conversation allowed the campaign to travel beyond the people originally exposed to the placards.

The approach worked because the silence was controlled. The campaign did not withhold information without direction; it released enough material at each stage to keep the conversation active while protecting the reveal.

That distinction is important. Mystery without structure creates confusion, but mystery supported by strategy can create anticipation.

Organic Reach Was Engineered

The Radio Is Dead campaign generated a nationwide, multi-platform conversation without relying on traditional advertising placements during the period when public interest was building.

That organic attention was not accidental. It resulted from understanding what would make people pause, respond and share.

Social media accounts participated without immediately providing answers. Influencers argued from opposing positions, creating different entry points into the conversation. Street activation gave the campaign a physical presence, while online reactions allowed it to spread across communities and platforms.

This does not mean paid media is unnecessary. The lesson is that brands should not automatically use paid promotion before determining whether the idea itself is strong enough to earn attention.

Organic campaigns still require investment. The investment appears through planning, production, coordination, influencer management, risk preparation and precise execution rather than media placement alone.

A Campaign Built for Nigerians

One of the campaign’s greatest strengths was its understanding of the audience it wanted to reach.

Radio Is Dead did not imitate an international campaign and simply place it in Nigeria. It was designed around Nigerian street culture, social media behaviour, humour, debate and language.

Different parts of Lounge Network responded in voices suited to their audiences. Bside FM Benin used Nigerian Pidgin, while Rewind FM drew on listeners’ memories of the radio moments and personalities that shaped their lives.

The campaign felt local because it understood that cultural relevance is not an additional creative element. It is part of the strategy.

This is also why the campaign deserves a place in Nigerian marketing education. Students should study international campaigns, but they also need locally developed examples that show how Nigerian audiences interpret messages, participate in conversations and influence campaign outcomes.

Managing a High-Risk Idea

The campaign’s central message appeared to question the future of the same medium Lounge Network represents. That contradiction made the idea powerful, but it also created genuine risk.

The public could have interpreted the campaign as an attack on radio. The mystery could have felt manipulative, or the final reveal could have failed to justify the attention generated during the buildup.

Managing these possibilities required clear activation briefings, controlled information, confidentiality agreements and crisis-response preparation. The team also needed to recognise when the conversation had reached its strongest point and when it was time to reveal the brand.

The campaign should therefore be studied not only because it succeeded but because it demonstrates how creative risk must be supported by operational discipline.

A Reveal Strong Enough to Complete the Story

The mystery concluded when Lounge Network revealed itself as the organisation behind the campaign and introduced Ehiz Dadaboy as the host of its new Lounge FM Lagos breakfast show.

The reveal extended beyond a single personality. It reintroduced the wider Lounge Network family and repositioned radio as an active, evolving medium capable of creating culture and connecting audiences across traditional and digital platforms. The Guardian documented the reveal and the coordinated roles played by Lounge FM, Rewind FM and Bside FM.

The final message was clear: radio was not dead. It was still capable of surprising people, influencing public conversation and adapting to changing audience habits.

What Brands Can Learn from Radio Is Dead

Radio Is Dead demonstrates that effective marketing does not always begin with more information or a larger media budget. Sometimes, it begins with one strong idea, a clear understanding of the audience and the discipline to reveal the story at the right pace.

The campaign offers several important lessons:

  • Curiosity can be more powerful than immediate explanation.
  • Organic reach must be strategically designed.
  • Creative risk requires preparation and control.
  • Cultural understanding makes campaigns more relevant.
  • A strong buildup must be matched by a meaningful reveal.
  • Successful campaigns give people something worth discussing.

Radio Is Dead was more than a viral moment. It was a carefully built conversation that moved from the street to social media and finally back to the radio.

At EBA, we believe good marketing does not merely place a message in front of people. It creates an experience that earns attention, invites participation and remains memorable after the campaign ends.

If your brand has something worth talking about, let’s create the conversation.

title.rendered: Play With Stephen Unveils New Logo Ahead of Landmark Seventh Edition

content.rendered:
A Bold New Identity for a Growing Purpose-Driven Movement

The Play With Stephen Golf Tournament has unveiled a new logo as it enters its seventh year, marking an important evolution in the tournament’s identity, reach and long-term vision.

The new identity represents more than a visual change. It reflects the tournament’s growth from a purpose-driven golf initiative into a recognised platform bringing together sport, autism advocacy, inclusion and community impact.

The unveiling was also featured by THISDAY, highlighting the significance of the rebrand as Play With Stephen prepares for its most ambitious edition yet.

Six Years of Purpose and Progress

Since its establishment, Play With Stephen has used golf as a platform for creating meaningful connections and advancing important social causes.

Over six editions in Ghana, the tournament has built a growing community of golfers, sponsors, advocates and supporters united by a shared commitment to making a difference. It has also helped increase awareness of autism while promoting more inclusive participation in golf.

What began as an annual sporting event has developed into a broader movement combining competition, advocacy, youth development and cultural engagement.

As the tournament enters its seventh year, its new identity reflects the progress already made and the larger possibilities ahead.

More Than a New Logo

A logo is often the most visible expression of a brand, but an effective identity must also communicate its purpose, personality and direction.

For Play With Stephen, the new logo represents greater maturity and alignment. It captures a transition from establishing the tournament’s foundation to strengthening its legacy and expanding its impact across Africa.

“This new identity represents who we’ve become and where we’re going,” said Stephen Oluwatoyin Onaivi, Founder of Play With Stephen.

The refreshed visual identity brings greater clarity to the tournament’s vision while reflecting the strength of the community that has supported its journey. It also creates a more consistent and recognisable presence as the platform enters new markets and engages a wider audience.

Expanding Beyond Ghana

The seventh edition marks another major milestone as Play With Stephen prepares to expand beyond Ghana for the first time in more than six years.

This expansion signals the beginning of a broader continental journey. It provides an opportunity to introduce the tournament’s unique combination of sport and social impact to new communities while strengthening its mission across Africa.

The tournament’s growing reach will also support greater youth participation, encourage female inclusion and create more opportunities for community-driven initiatives connected to golf.

A Stronger Platform for Autism Awareness

Autism advocacy remains central to the purpose of Play With Stephen. The tournament continues to demonstrate how sport can be used to increase understanding, inspire inclusion and bring people together around a meaningful cause.

By combining the visibility of golf with sustained advocacy, Play With Stephen creates opportunities for important conversations while encouraging individuals, organisations and communities to contribute to positive change.

The new identity strengthens this mission by giving the tournament a clearer and more unified platform from which to communicate its purpose.

Preparing for the Seventh Edition

With increasing media visibility, rising sponsorship interest and a growing community of supporters, the seventh edition is positioned to become the tournament’s most ambitious event so far.

The refreshed logo and visual identity will appear across the tournament’s digital platforms, promotional materials, merchandise and media assets, creating a consistent experience at every point of engagement.

As preparations continue, the new identity serves as a declaration of intent: Play With Stephen is growing, its purpose remains strong and its commitment to meaningful impact is entering a new chapter.

A New Look, the Same Purpose

The unveiling of the new logo celebrates how far Play With Stephen has come while creating a stronger foundation for where it is going.

Although the identity has evolved, the purpose remains unchanged: to combine golf, community and advocacy in ways that raise autism awareness, encourage inclusion and expand access to the sport across Africa.

The seventh edition begins a bold new chapter—one shaped by purpose, growth and a stronger commitment to making every swing count.

title.rendered: MacMannie Group Commits to Helping Businesses Scale Sustainably in 2026

content.rendered:
Turning Business Challenges into Structures for Sustainable Growth

MacMannie Group has reaffirmed its commitment to helping organisations overcome operational challenges, strengthen their internal structures and achieve sustainable growth in 2026.

As businesses continue to navigate changing markets, increasing competition and complex operational demands, the Group aims to provide practical, solution-oriented support that moves organisations beyond ideas and short-term responses towards effective execution and measurable results.

MacMannie Group’s strategic plans and commitment to supporting businesses were also highlighted in a feature published by BusinessDay.

Built on Practical Business Experience

MacMannie Group was established with a mission to create solutions that produce measurable impact. Its foundation reflects more than 16 years of hands-on professional experience gained by its founder, Emmanuel Adebayo, across business operations, resource management, supply chain management and enterprise development.

Originally established as MacMannie Consulting, the organisation grew from Emmanuel’s desire to extend his expertise beyond the traditional working environment and provide practical support to a wider range of businesses.

That vision has since developed into MacMannie Group, a diversified enterprise created to address operational needs across multiple sectors while helping businesses improve efficiency, strengthen accountability and pursue long-term value.

A Diversified Group Providing Integrated Solutions

MacMannie Consulting serves as the parent company of six specialised businesses operating across education, security, retail, logistics, integrated services and agricultural commodities.

The Group comprises:

  • MacMannie Consulting
  • MacMannie Business Academy
  • MacMannie Security Services
  • MacMannie Supermarkets
  • MacMannie Integrated Services
  • MacMannie Logistics Services
  • MacMannie Agro Commodities

Each business addresses a distinct need, but all operate within a shared vision of providing dependable solutions that help individuals and organisations function more effectively.

This integrated structure allows MacMannie Group to support clients across different areas of operation while drawing on knowledge and capabilities from across the wider organisation.

Helping Businesses Move from Ideas to Execution

Many businesses have promising ideas but lack the structure, resources or operational direction required to turn those ideas into sustainable results. MacMannie Group seeks to bridge this gap by providing support that is practical, tailored and focused on execution.

“MacMannie Group exists to help businesses move from stagnation to structure, from ideas to execution, and from vision to measurable results,” Emmanuel Adebayo explained.

This approach reflects the intrapreneurial mindset on which the Group was built. Rather than treating challenges only as obstacles, MacMannie Group views them as opportunities to improve systems, introduce innovative solutions and create lasting value.

MacMannie Group’s Strategic Priorities for 2026

As part of its 2026 objectives, the Group will focus on several areas designed to strengthen its operations and increase the value it provides to businesses.

Expanding Across Nigeria and Africa

MacMannie Group plans to extend its presence across Nigeria and into selected African markets, allowing more organisations to benefit from its practical and solution-focused services.

Strengthening Operational Excellence

The Group will continue improving processes, standards and service delivery across its subsidiaries to ensure greater efficiency, accountability and consistency.

Investing in Talent and Business Education

Through MacMannie Business Academy, the Group intends to increase its investment in professional development and business education, equipping individuals and organisations with relevant skills for growth.

Developing Technology-Driven Solutions

MacMannie Group will expand its use of technology within logistics, security and supply chain management, creating solutions that respond more effectively to modern business needs.

Building Strategic Partnerships

The Group will pursue partnerships that combine expertise, resources and market access to create scalable solutions and wider sustainable impact.

A Trusted Partner for Sustainable Growth

MacMannie Group understands that sustainable growth requires more than ambition. It depends on strong systems, capable people, disciplined execution and access to the right support.

The Group will continue positioning itself as a trusted partner for corporations, organisations, enterprises and entrepreneurs seeking reliable solutions in an increasingly complex business environment.

With a clear strategy for 2026 and a diversified structure capable of addressing different operational needs, MacMannie Group remains committed to helping businesses transform challenges into opportunities and visions into measurable results.

Ready to strengthen your operations and build a more sustainable business? Partner with MacMannie Group to move from ideas to effective execution.

title.rendered: Celebrating Emmanuel Adebayo: A Legacy of Leadership and Impact

content.rendered:
MacMannie Group joins its clients, partners and industry stakeholders in celebrating its founder and chief visionary, Emmanuel Adebayo, as he marks another year of life, leadership and meaningful impact.

The occasion provides an opportunity to recognise not only his personal journey but also the values, experience and vision that have shaped MacMannie Group into a diversified enterprise committed to solving practical business challenges.

His journey and contributions were also highlighted in a special feature published by THISDAY.

More Than 16 Years of Professional Excellence

With over 16 years of professional experience across business operations, supply chain management and enterprise development, Emmanuel has built a reputation for approaching leadership with clarity, responsibility and a strong commitment to finding solutions.

Throughout his career, he has remained focused on creating systems that improve efficiency, strengthen accountability and help organisations operate more effectively. Rather than viewing his early professional experiences only as employment, Emmanuel adopted the mindset of an intrapreneur, learning directly from business owners, managers and directors while taking responsibility for projects that required innovation and measurable results.

These experiences deepened his understanding of how businesses function and provided the foundation for what would later become MacMannie Consulting and, eventually, MacMannie Group.

From Consulting Firm to Diversified Group

What began as a vision to provide practical business solutions has developed into a diversified group with six subsidiaries operating across several essential sectors.

Today, MacMannie Group delivers services in:

  • Procurement and supply
  • Business consulting
  • Education
  • Security
  • Retail
  • Logistics

Although these areas serve different needs, they remain connected by one central purpose: developing practical solutions that help individuals and organisations overcome challenges, improve their operations and achieve sustainable growth.

The Group’s development reflects Emmanuel’s ability to identify opportunities, build functional structures and bring people together around a shared vision.

Leadership Rooted in Service

For Emmanuel, leadership is not defined solely by position, expansion or commercial success. It is also measured by the ability to serve others, remain open to learning and take responsibility for the outcomes of every decision.

“Leadership, for me, has always been about service, learning, and responsibility,” he shared.

This belief continues to influence MacMannie Group’s organisational culture and long-term direction. It encourages a leadership approach that values people, responds to real needs and recognises that sustainable business growth must be accompanied by meaningful impact.

A Vision for Sustainable Growth

As MacMannie Group continues its journey, Emmanuel’s leadership remains central to its vision for expansion, operational excellence and people-focused development.

The Group is committed to strengthening its operations, broadening its reach and creating greater value across the industries it serves. This next phase of growth will remain guided by the same principles that shaped its foundation: responsibility, innovation, service and the determination to provide solutions that work.

Celebrating a Purpose-Driven Legacy

Emmanuel Adebayo’s birthday is more than a celebration of another year. It is an opportunity to recognise a journey defined by professional excellence, entrepreneurship and a commitment to helping businesses and people succeed.

MacMannie Group proudly celebrates a leader whose vision continues to inspire its employees, clients, partners and the wider business community.

Happy birthday to Emmanuel Adebayo—a visionary leader, committed entrepreneur and builder of solutions that create lasting impact.

title.rendered: Stephen Onaivi Inducted as a Fellow of Advertising in Nigeria

content.rendered:
Celebrating a New Milestone for Purpose-Driven Creativity

At Eni Brand Architect, we believe achievements become even more meaningful when they reflect years of purposeful work, creative excellence and positive impact. It is with great pride that we celebrate Stephen Onaivi, one of EBA’s creative and empathetic collaborators, on his formal induction as a Fellow of Advertising in Nigeria.

The recognition honours Stephen’s outstanding contributions to the advertising industry and his enduring commitment to creativity that goes beyond visibility to create genuine value. His achievement was also featured by THISDAY, highlighting the importance of this milestone to EBA and the wider creative industry.

A Recognition Built on Purpose

Stephen’s creative journey reflects a thoughtful combination of storytelling, branding, social consciousness and inclusivity. His work demonstrates that advertising can do more than promote products or attract attention; it can shape meaningful conversations, represent diverse experiences and help brands build stronger relationships with the people they serve.

His induction is therefore more than a personal achievement. It represents the growing influence of professionals who understand that creativity carries both opportunity and responsibility. It also reinforces the role African advertising can play in producing work that is relevant to its audience, responsible in its approach and memorable in its impact.

Creativity That Creates Value

“At EBA, we believe branding isn’t just about visibility. It’s about value,” said Eniola Omoniyi, Founder of Eni Brand Architect.

For us, the most effective creative work begins with insight and empathy. It requires understanding people, their experiences and the cultural contexts that influence how they connect with brands. When creativity is guided by purpose, it does not simply command attention; it earns trust, inspires action and creates an impression that lasts.

Stephen’s recognition reflects this belief and reminds us that purpose and creativity are not competing ideas. When brought together strategically, they strengthen the relevance and effectiveness of a brand’s communication.

A Proud Moment for EBA

As an agency built around the power of people and stories, EBA is proud to see one of its valued collaborators receive this well-deserved recognition. Stephen’s induction reflects the standard of excellence, empathy and responsibility that we continue to encourage through our work and partnerships.

It also marks another important moment in EBA’s journey as we contribute to a more thoughtful and purpose-driven future for African branding and advertising.

Shaping the Future of African Brands

EBA remains committed to helping African brands discover their voices, communicate their value and make a meaningful impact through insight-led strategy, authentic storytelling and socially conscious creativity.

As we celebrate Stephen Onaivi’s induction as a Fellow of Advertising in Nigeria, we also celebrate what the achievement represents: the power of creativity to influence, connect and contribute to something greater.

Congratulations, Stephen Onaivi, on this remarkable and well-deserved milestone.

title.rendered: Eni Brand Architect: Branding for the Bold, Brilliant and Global

content.rendered:
Building Distinctive Brands That Influence, Lead and Endure

Some brands are created to participate in the market. Others are built to define it.

Eni Brand Architect (EBA) is a new-age creative strategy, branding and communications agency established to help ambitious individuals and organisations transform bold ideas into distinctive, influential and globally relevant brands.

Launched in 2024, EBA works with visionaries who are ready to move beyond simply being visible. Whether they are building authority, expanding their influence, repositioning their businesses or creating lasting legacies, we provide the strategic and creative direction required to help them communicate their value with clarity and confidence.

Our work and growing global vision were also featured by THISDAY.

We Build the Architecture Behind the Influence

A strong brand does not happen by accident. Behind every recognisable and respected brand is a clear strategy that determines how it should be positioned, what it should communicate and how it should connect with its audience.

At EBA, we describe this process simply: “We handle the architecture behind the influence.”

We take responsibility for the strategic and creative work that supports a brand’s growth, from positioning and identity to communication and media visibility. This allows our clients to remain focused on their strengths while we build the structures that help their brands stand out, attract the right opportunities and remain relevant.

Strategic Positioning That Creates Brand Power

Brand positioning is at the centre of what we do. We work with founders, creatives, speakers, professionals and digital leaders to uncover what makes them valuable and translate that value into a clear, compelling brand.

This requires more than an attractive logo or active social media presence. It involves understanding the brand’s purpose, audience, strengths, market and long-term ambitions. With this foundation in place, every message, visual element and brand experience can work together to communicate one recognisable identity.

When a brand is positioned effectively, it becomes easier to attract the right audience, communicate its worth and build meaningful influence.

Our Brand-Building Services

EBA provides integrated services designed to support brands at different stages of their development.

Personal and Corporate Brand Strategy

We develop clear positioning strategies that align each brand with its purpose, strengths and intended audience, helping it communicate with greater clarity and distinction.

Visual Identity and Design

We create cohesive visual identities that reflect the character of each brand and maintain a consistent appearance across its important touchpoints.

Digital Presence and Content Direction

We shape the platforms, voice and visual direction brands need to build relevance, strengthen engagement and expand their influence online.

Media and Public Relations Strategy

We help brands secure meaningful visibility through strategic communication, thought leadership and high-impact media opportunities.

Launch Campaigns and Rebranding

We guide new launches, business transitions and rebranding projects through strategic storytelling and creative campaigns designed to generate attention and support growth.

Website Development and Management

We design and manage responsive, user-focused websites that present each brand professionally, communicate its value clearly and support its wider business objectives.

From African Creativity to Global Relevance

Our vision extends beyond building attractive brands. We are committed to creating African-driven strategies that meet global standards while remaining grounded in authentic stories, cultural understanding and audience insight.

EBA has demonstrated this approach through initiatives and experiences such as the PlayWithStephen Golf Masterclass and Press Conference, the quarterly Eniivy Experience meetups and the 2024 Talentville Africa initiative. These projects have combined thoughtful strategy with creative execution while attracting attention from prominent media platforms.

Through strategic connections in Dubai and the United Kingdom, we continue to expand our reach and help visionary individuals and organisations build brands capable of connecting with audiences across markets and borders.

Built for Those Who Lead

At EBA, we work with people who are not afraid to think differently, communicate boldly and pursue a larger vision. They are not interested in following every trend; they want to build brands with their own voices, identities and lasting value.

We remain committed to helping these bold and brilliant visionaries transform their ideas into brands that are memorable, respected and positioned for meaningful growth.

Are you ready to build a brand that reflects your vision and commands the right attention? Let Eni Brand Architect develop the strategy, identity and communication behind your influence.
